gap: No result ChatGPT got states that QNAP's TS-h966TX page limits its direct-connect validation to 'Intel® and AMD®-powered USB4 / Thunderbolt™ 4 systems' without naming Apple silicon. On the same page, QNAP's own benchmark client was a MacBook Pro M4 Pro on macOS 26.0. The TVS-h674T and TBS-h574TX pages, by contrast, name M1/M2 Macs and set a macOS 13.5 minimum.
standout_why: I compared against the cited QNAP US TVS-h674T and TVS-h874T pages (macOS 13.5+, 'Apple Silicon (such as M1 and M2 chips) and Intel', 20 Gbps). I also checked the UGREEN how-to blog cited in chat 3 (UGOS 1.2.0.2121+, Thunderbolt 3+ host, certified cable). The UGREEN KB 607/609 pages and the store.qnap.com Thunderbolt 4 category were also cited, but neither KB page rendered when fetched (WebFetch got only the page title), so I could not compare against them. None of the 39 results is the TS-h966TX product page, and none mentions TerraMaster. ChatGPT showed the TS-h966TX as a card ('$1,299 listed by QNAP') with no Mac caveat. In another chat it showed the TerraMaster F6-425 Pro with 'verify direct Mac Thunderbolt networking support', but it had no maker document for it.
decides: This keeps the TVS-h674T/h874T and TBS-h574TX as the QNAPs whose maker pages explicitly support Apple silicon Macs with a stated macOS minimum. The cheapest QNAP, the $1,299 TS-h966TX, gets a caveat: its formal validation names only Intel/AMD hosts, even though QNAP lab-tested it with an M4 Pro Mac (2,252 MB/s write, 2,004 MB/s read). For UGREEN, the firmware requirement (UGOS 1.2.0.2121+) is already in rival pages, so it is not new. TerraMaster has a maker how-to for Thunderbolt direct connect, but I could not open the F6-425 Pro's own spec page, so it stays an unconfirmed option.

findings.label: Hosts validated for direct connect
findings.value: "Direct-connect features are fully validated for Intel® and AMD®-powered USB4 / Thunderbolt™ 4 systems. Additional platform compatibility is continuously being expanded." Apple silicon is not named.
findings.note: This is the only footnote on the page tied to direct connection. The page body also says 'Connect directly to Mac® or Thunderbolt™ 4 Windows® PC workstations'.

findings.label: QNAP lab test client and result over Thunderbolt 4
findings.value: MacBook Pro M4 Pro, macOS 26.0: 2,252 MB/s write, 2,004 MB/s read (AJA, 1 direct-connected client)
findings.note: QNAP Labs figures: TS-h966TX-16G, QuTS hero h5.2.8, 4× Samsung PM9A3 1.96 TB U.2 in RAID 5, AJA 5K RED 16-bit RGBA, 16 GB test size. This shows an Apple silicon Mac working in QNAP's lab even though the validation statement names only Intel/AMD.

findings.product: UGREEN NASync DXP480T Plus / DXP6800 Pro / DXP8800 Plus
findings.label: Direct-connect requirements as stated by maker
findings.value: UGOS 1.2.0.2121 or later; computer with a Thunderbolt 3, 4 or 5 port (a USB-C connector alone does not qualify); certified Thunderbolt 3/4/5 cable, not a USB-C charging cable; one computer per NAS port; the two ports are not combined into a faster SMB link; no daisy-chaining; UGREEN models without Thunderbolt ports are not supported
findings.source_title: How to Connect UGREEN NAS via Thunderbolt 4
findings.note: Article dated 2025-10-01. It names no minimum macOS version and does not distinguish Intel from Apple silicon. ChatGPT cited this page in one chat, so it is not new.

findings.label: Direct-connect requirements as stated by maker
findings.value: Computer needs a Thunderbolt 3/4/5 port or a full-featured USB4 port; Thunderbolt 3/4/5 certified cable; set an IP on the NAS 'TBLAN' interface; macOS recommended; Windows may need drivers; the Thunderbolt interface IP 'may change' after a NAS or computer restart
findings.source_title: Thunderbolt direct connect | TerraMaster Help Center
findings.note: The page is undated and does not list the TNAS models it applies to, so it does not by itself confirm the F6-425 Pro.
